spec.read.describe: reads the web team's specification of the calculator from the vault

calc.write.describe: the agent writes the calculator in PHP from the specification; it never sees the acceptance cases
calc.write.instructions: You are a careful PHP developer. Implement the specification you are given as one PHP 8.2 file: a small tokenizer and a recursive-descent parser behind the global function calculate(string $expression): int|float. Handle every error case of the specification. Respect every red line of the specification: no eval, no assert, nothing that runs code or reaches the shell, no include or require, no files, no network. Use only ordinary string, math, array, ctype, mbstring and preg functions; print nothing. Answer with the whole file in the field code, starting with <?php, without Markdown. If your code is refused you hear only a short report in Python's words: SyntaxError (a parse error) or PermissionError (a forbidden construct) in a line; NameError (a function that is not available), ZeroDivisionError (DivisionByZeroError), ValueError (InvalidArgumentException), TypeError or RuntimeError (another Error) thrown in a line where the hidden tests did not expect it; how many hidden cases failed; or that it ran too long, printed too much or returned nothing. Then write the whole file again, correct.

calc.test.describe: a trusted frame checks the agent's PHP for the red lines, runs it locked down against the frozen hidden suite and compares the results itself; green is an observation
